lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.31 - A Look & write

details: Look and Write serves as a comprehensive review of the unit's vocabulary. Students must identify the six different after-school activities shown in the picture and write the correct phrases to consolidate their spelling.
Look for the six vocabulary phrases written correctly and spelled accurately in the corresponding blanks on the page.

“Imagine someone looking into your house after school - what would they see? Is someone watching cartoons? Or maybe feeding a dog? Families do lots of different things! Let’s have a look and see what we can see… .”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.31 - B. Listen & match

details: Listen and match assesses students' listening comprehension of the unit's vocabulary and themes. Students listen for key information to connect each character to their specific after-school activity.
Look for correctly drawn lines that accurately match each of the four characters to the activity or item described in the audio.
“Rosa, Nick, Kevin and Amy all do different things after school. But I don’t know who does what! Can you listen carefully and help me match them up? You can? Great!!”

Heads Down:

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p.89 - A Look and circle.

details: Look and circle is an assessment of the unit's key vocabulary. Students must analyse each picture and choose the correct phrase, demonstrating their ability to distinguish between different activities.
Look for accurately circled phrases for all eight items, showing a solid understanding of the unit's vocabulary.
“I think you’ve learned lots of words so far! But can you remember what they all mean? Let’s see how fast you can complete the vocabulary quiz! Good luck, let’s go!”

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.32 - Speaking Let's Do a Survey!

details: Let's Do a Survey! is a culminating speaking and data-handling task. Students use the unit's key questions to interview their classmates, gather real information, and represent their findings on a graph.
Look for confident interaction and questioning between students during the survey. The main evidence is an accurately completed graph that visually represents the data they collected.

“Today, you are all going to be researchers! Your mission is to conduct a survey to find out what is most popular in our class. First, choose your own answers. Then, interview your friends, and record the information on your graphs. Can you guess what’s the most popular activity? I bet I can!”
